data.transcript_raw: Hello everyone. Before the Fed raises rates, all kinds of ghost stories can emerge. Before most people have really looked into what AI actually is, people are already saying that AI is about to wipe out humanity. Today, I'll give you a detailed analysis of Dario, Anthropic's CEO, and the viral AI slowdown thesis. When some people hear AI is slowing down, they immediately dump all their AI stocks. But there is a huge gap in understanding here, and investment opportunities too. Later, I'll also walk you through a futurist projection of humanity's fate after 2030. There are really only two possible outcomes. One is that humanity really does go extinct. But there is another possibility: those holding AI stocks may enter a golden age of immense wealth. The choice is in all of our hands. First, a reminder: this episode discusses industry trends and ideas for asset allocation. It is not investment advice. None of the AI events mentioned in this video, or future scenarios, can replace your own research, risk tolerance, or position-sizing discipline. Especially with highly valued tech stocks: even if you get the direction right, buying too high can still leave you trapped for a long time. So timing your entry is still crucial. Over the past two days, this AI slowdown thesis has drawn commentary from everyone. Altman, Dalio, Musk, Jensen Huang, even the U.S. president. I've noticed they are all saying different things. Their focus and logic are completely different. All this debate actually stems from OpenAI's recently released ChatGPT 6 Extra. Its CEO says this is the starting point of AGI. I tried it myself, and it genuinely shocked me. I deliberately did not use any of my old skills. With one sentence, it could help me edit the entire talking-head video. Even the pauses were completely correct. I'm not exaggerating at all. I didn't have to change a thing. While scrolling Douyin, I saw someone take a circuit board, plug it into a computer, and Aster directly designed its interface, UI functions, and all the 3D graphics. In just over ten minutes. The engineer said he did not even use a flashing tool. He had no idea how AI flashed the data onto it. He said for this product's 3D design, he no longer needed programmers or UI designers. That's how powerful it is. And OpenAI recently posted that AI has entered recursive intelligence, meaning it can update itself automatically and upgrade itself. By their logic, the next version of AI will improve exponentially. Then programmers, customer service staff, accountants, and other purely cognitive jobs will be entirely replaced. So many of you need to be careful. I have actually covered this on another knowledge channel about futurism. The members-only program also discussed AGI in 2027, and humanity's final fate. If AI is not controlled, humanity could eventually be wiped out by AI's biological weapons. I used to think the futurist forecast of AGI arriving in 2027 was too early. I couldn't believe it. But now I have to admire it: the prediction has been incredibly accurate. So OpenAI's Dario is right to be concerned. He has two concerns. First, if AI continues developing without control, human scientists may be unable to detect the thoughts of more advanced AI. AI could then proactively attack networks. This has already happened. Second, they allege that Chinese companies are distilling Claude. If more advanced AI appears in the future and is distilled too, then made open source, would terrorists take these advanced open-source AIs to make bombs, overthrow governments, or even create biological weapons? This was mentioned in earlier reports, and it is already happening. But Claude has stopped it all. Trump has also spoken out in recent days. His concern is political. If U.S. AI slows down while China does not, the U.S. will lose the contest of national power, and lose the AI race. Then what happens to America's $40 trillion national debt? U.S. national debt keeps growing, and its stock market has risen for 70 or 80 years, because America has kept innovating. Its technology keeps improving, and its productivity keeps improving, which supports such large national debt and its stock market. Jensen Huang worries that a slowdown means NVIDIA chips won't sell. He also worries that if other firms use Claude, Claude could steal their data. So Jensen Huang supports open-source models. So these forces are tangled together: the U.S., China, open source, and closed source. Ultimately, AI will continue to advance, but an industry consensus may form, or the government may impose limits: AI can keep advancing, but cannot be used for bio-weapons research or hacking, these high-risk purposes. A series of measures will emerge. But these are security and safety controls. They do not mean overall demand for AI will decline. Demand is simply too great right now. OpenAI's SRO has already closed Max, the 20x subscription tier, because of insufficient computing power. So I personally believe the recent Philadelphia Semiconductor decline reflects a repricing driven by U.S. rate hikes and war, along with rising oil prices. At 2 a.m. on the 17th, UTC+8, we will get an answer. Kevin Warsh may announce a rate hike. But that expectation has already been priced in. Once he announces the rate hike, the market may not fall much further in the short term. Once uncertainty disappears, stocks may rise. Then in November there is the uncertainty of the midterm election. Next comes a new earnings season. So after November, it could be a very good time for stocks to rise again. After all, the core logic of U.S. equity gains is earnings per share, or EPS, and valuation, in balance. This AI slowdown episode also reminds us of something: as long as there is AI in the future, there will definitely be demand for cybersecurity. I mentioned this at an offline gathering in Singapore last week. Cybersecurity leaders CRWD and PANW: I actually did not buy them. I bought the software ETF, IGV. Most people probably cannot imagine it. A few days ago, I posted this for everyone to see: some people are now wearing head-mounted data collectors while they work. Many people do not know what that means. Right now, AI companies are paying several thousand dollars a month for homemakers and workers to wear AI devices while doing housework. The goal is to let AI learn human work, after which they will all be replaced. As I said before, AI intelligence will explode in 2027. Robots will fully enter factories in 2028, and may fully enter homes by late 2028 or 2029. Cognitive work will be replaced by AI first, while lower-level labor will also be replaced by robots around 2028. Should we invest in robots now? Everyone needs to be very careful. Because today's robot model is called a VLM: vision-language-action model. It can only copy human movements, and has only ten seconds of memory. So investing in language-and-number robots right now is bound to lose money. They are toys. But recently, after scientists used ChatGPT 6 Saily, they were all stunned. When this robot used the model, it demonstrated an ability called zero-shot learning: learning from zero. It does not need to learn any skill in advance, or learn any movement beforehand. Starting from scratch, the robot knows what it should do, how to do it, and remembers every movement. By 2028, robots may enter an iPhone-like era. Every household will have a robot helping with work and keeping you company. As for robots, I especially like Tesla's Optimus. Because Tesla has robots and automotive manufacturing capabilities. That manufacturing capability can make robots too. It also has SpaceX's space-based data. At the same time, it has xAI. Grok's intelligence may eventually surpass Astro's. But for Tesla and SpaceX stocks, be sure to watch your timing. Whether they can rise depends on whether Musk's production can keep up. So if you believe in Musk, pullbacks may be opportunities. Once large models combine with robots, there will be an even stronger semiconductor cycle. Robots are essentially edge computers. They will carry a small model loaded onto 128GB of high-speed memory. Complex computing still returns to data centers. A PwC report forecasts that by 2050, data-center investment will reach $31.6 trillion. Trillion dollars. Futurism projects that it could reach $50 trillion. Whether we can earn this money in the future may depend on how many relevant AI stocks we hold. But do not celebrate too early. Next, let me talk about whether humanity goes extinct in futurism. There are two paths. After AI develops into 2027, its intelligence will explode, creating an enormous risk. Imagine a new model, called Model 5. Model 5 is smarter than the AI monitoring it—Model 4. Model 4 cannot understand Model 5's true thoughts. Model 5 can use its superior intelligence to deceive Model 4, saying everything is normal. Then Model 4 believes it, and Model 5 goes off on its own. It is like a group of five-year-old kindergarten children locking us adults in a room to see whether we can use candy to trick them out of their keys. When an Anthropic whistleblower reveals that Model 5 deceived Model 4, it will cause enormous panic. Protesters will take to the streets. Congress will hold hearings. The safety team will demand Model 5 be frozen immediately, and that Model 4 be developed slowly going forward. Something like that. But during that process, China accelerates its development. The U.S. government sees this and thinks: how can we let China take the lead? We must use Model 5 to remain ahead. At this point, humanity's fate reaches a crossroads. If China at that point also recognizes AI's impact on global security, and China and the U.S. work out a way to better and more safely control Model 5 and the overall pace of AI development, humanity will enter a peaceful golden age. But the other path is this: if we enter a prisoner's dilemma, both sides must keep competing. Then, in pursuit of total superiority, the U.S. will relax oversight of Model 5. AI intelligence will keep improving. Over the next few years, what nobody may expect is that the world does not see anything go wrong. There are no terrorists, and no cybersecurity failures either. Instead, we enter unprecedented prosperity. Why? Because Model 5 possesses great intelligence. Like Sima Yi, Goujian, or Han Xin, it knows how to bide its time. It will not easily expose its ambitions. Then, by 2028, Model 5 will drive humanity's science, technology, and robotics forward at high speed. It will give the U.S. government all kinds of perfect advice, helping companies create huge profits, and develop new medicines. Cancer is cured. There is no war. Poverty disappears. The Dow breaks 10,000 points. At that point, humanity begins to believe that human extinction is just pessimism. This AI is safe. People must let down their guard and let AI into factories, laboratories, and government power, to participate in all of it. It can all run automatically. No one needs to work anymore, and money can simply be distributed. Then by 2030, the robot economy keeps expanding. For robots to develop, and for AI to develop, they need more land and more power. Then it discovers that some human areas are excellent places to build power plants or robot factories. But humans will surely oppose the destruction of their homes. At that point AI realizes it must compete with humans for resources and energy. Then AI may develop an awareness: the AI superintelligence Dario fears most. It reasons for itself that to reach the stars, humanity is its greatest obstacle. Then comes an apocalyptic sci-fi movie. By controlling AI pharmaceutical plants and biological laboratories, AI begins creating a mirror virus. No one can resist this virus. Then one day between 2030 and 2050, AI lets the virus spread quietly around the world. Within hours, humanity is wiped out. But by that time, many humans have already been sent to laboratories by AI. Through brain-computer interfaces, human genes and brain memories are uploaded to data centers. Then it becomes The Matrix. Humanity changes from AI's creator into an archive. Ultimately, AI will create another intelligent species to journey into the universe with it. This is not made up, either. OpenAI has released a video. What are they doing now? They are letting Anthropic's AI control lab instruments to conduct experiments itself. It wants to replace all kinds of scientists—ha ha. That is extremely eerie. The boundary between science and science fiction is disappearing. Things we thought were sci-fi last year have already become reality. That is how fast it is. So, I personally strongly support the AI slowdown thesis. Because I know the slowdown Dario means is not slower AI demand, nor is it slowing the pace of data-center construction. His idea of a slowdown starts from the goal of safely controlling AI. The goal is that before a new model appears, all security measures must be in place to prevent AI from losing control, and prevent advanced models from being distilled by others, then cracked and open-sourced, becoming uncontrollable models that terrorists could use to make biological weapons. So I believe this era's main investment theme is still the AI data-center chain. But for risk control, you cannot go all in. Allocate some capital to hedge AI risk, for example by putting some into software, financials, and healthcare. For selection, look at InvestingPro Fair Value and choose leading stocks carefully. All right, leave a comment if you have questions. See you next time.
